title: Father Goriot, Balzac
subject: litterature
description: Goriot sacrifices everything for his ungrateful daughters. Rastignac learns about Paris on the back of a father and a convict. Balzac invents the Human Comedy.

hero.hook: A sordid pension, a father who dies alone, and a young man who challenges Paris from a cemetery.

blocks.text: Published in **1835**, **Father Goriot** is the pivot of , a project by **Honoré de Balzac**: nearly 90 interconnected novels describing all of French society. This is where he introduces the return of characters from one book to another. **[[The Human Comedy]]**

Three residents of the **House Vauquer** embody the tensions between the provinces and Paris, fortune and morality, innocence and cynicism. The novel is a lesson about money, ambition and family betrayal. Balzac shows how Paris “corrupts” those who come there to seek glory.

**Honoré de Balzac** wants to archive all the social types of his time in **90 novels** and **2,000 characters**. A protagonist from one book reappears in another, creating quasi-historical depth. It is a major innovation of the 19th century novel.

blocks.caption: Honoré de Balzac: the obsessed archivist of 19th century France.

blocks.text: Balzac ordered his custom-made coffee makers. It is estimated that he drank around 50,000 cups of coffee during his life as a night shift worker.

In Balzac, we always know where each character's money comes from. The budget is the secret engine of human drama. He observed the **Monarchy of July**, from 1830 to 1848, a time when money gradually replaced noble birth.

**Jean-Joachim Goriot**, former vermicelli maker, pasta manufacturer, sacrificed everything for his daughters **Anastasia** and **Delphine**. He moves down from floor to floor at the **pension Vauquer** as his resources run out.

blocks.caption: The Vauquer pension: social microcosm of Parisian poverty.

blocks.text: His daughters, locked in the demands of , Parisian high society with ruthless codes, only come back to ask for money. Goriot dies alone while they go to the ball. Balzac makes him a Christ-like figure, a total sacrifice for ungrateful beings. **[[World]]**

**Eugène de Rastignac**, an ambitious young provincial, discovers that merit alone is not enough in Paris. , escaped convict and criminal genius, offers him a cynical pact: make his fortune through murder. **[[Vautrin (Jacques Collin)]]**

blocks.attribution: Honoré de Balzac, Father Goriot — Rastignac

blocks.text: Rastignac refuses crime, but his conscience is dulled by contact with salons. Goriot's death acts as a final revealer. From the **Père-Lachaise** cemetery, he launches his challenge to Paris. Balzac is buried today in this exact location.

Balzac makes the place a psychological engine: the musty smell of the Vauquer pension prepares moral misery. This theory of the environment, where the environment shapes the characters, announces the **naturalism** of **Émile Zola**, a movement which pushes realism towards scientific description. Money breaks up families under the July Monarchy. The novel remains an essential part of understanding 19th century Paris.

By creating Rastignac and Vautrin, Balzac offers European culture archetypes to read provincial ambition and Parisian cynicism. The novel doesn't just paint lives: it maps a system where money and rank eat feelings. **Rastignac** will return in around twenty works of the Comédie humaine, proof that Balzac already thought of his universe as a series.

events.title: Publication
events.detail: The central novel of the Human Comedy.

blocks.text: **Father Goriot**, published in **1835**, inaugurates the return of the characters and the figure of Rastignac, who challenges Paris by accepting the social struggle without the gloves of morality.
